items.title: Serve Robotics launches new business to become the AWS for robots | TechCrunch
items.summary:
Serve Robotics, a maker of self-driving sidewalk delivery robots, is expanding beyond its autonomous delivery operations in a bid to become a technology supplier to other companies building robots.

The company, which spun out of Uber’s acquisition of Postmates in 2021 and went public in 2024, said Thursday it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services. [...] Specifically, Serve Robotics will offer customers its connectivity and data tools. Bedrock Robotics, a startup developing self-driving systems for construction equipment, is a customer, according to Serve. It’s also working with T-Mobile to bring AI computing power closer to robots, Serve announced alongside its third-quarter earnings on Thursday.

“We are solving the problem of robots in human spaces,” Serve Robotics CEO and co-founder Ai Kashani told TechCrunch. [...] Serve Robotics already makes two kinds of robots, the cute googly-eyed sidewalk delivery robot and one designed for hospitals that it got through its acquisition of Diligent Robotics.

Those businesses are not going away, Kashani emphasized in a recent interview. Instead, he said there is opportunity to sell the technology it developed for its own robots to other companies developing robots for farms, warehouses, and other uncontrolled environments.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

Look at the sign behind her: "CROTTIE JON". "Toocenean".

That is not a company. That is AI spelling. The robot girl is a video prompt, not a product.

But the real robots got crazy cheap 👇

📉 THE PRICE OF A HUMANOID

2023 → Unitree H1: about $90,000
2024 → Unitree G1: about $16,000
2025 → Unitree R1: $5,900
2026 → R1 from about $4,300 in China, sold worldwide on AliExpress

From luxury car to used car in 3 years.

🏦 WHAT WALL STREET SAW

🔵 Goldman Sachs
In one year, the cost to build a humanoid fell about 40%. From $50K-$250K to $30K-$150K.
Goldman expected 15-20% a year.
Its 2035 market forecast jumped 6x: from $6B to $38B.

🟠 Morgan Stanley
More than 1 billion humanoids by 2050. A $5 trillion market.
Price per robot: from about $200K in 2024 to $50K in 2050.
About 90% of them for factories and shops, not homes.

🔴 The catch
The cheap R1 is 1.22 m tall, weighs 25 kg and runs about an hour per battery.
It is made for developers. It will not fold your laundry.
The robots that work in factories still cost tens of thousands.

💡 THE LESSON

A fake robot girl now costs one prompt.
A real robot costs less than a used car.

The video got perfect first. The robot is catching up on price.
Usefulness is the last thing left to fix.

items.title: The Princeton professor who also works as a research scientist at Google DeepMind is uploading an entire robotics course
items.summary:
The Princeton professor who also works as a research scientist at Google DeepMind is uploading an entire robotics course to YouTube this fall, and the full previous run is already online: 24 lectures, about 29 hours, free.

"Introduction to Robotics," Anirudha Majumdar (@Majumdar_Ani), Princeton.

motion planning and RRTs, quadrotor dynamics, PD control and LQR, Bayes, Kalman and particle filters, SLAM, optical flow, then deep learning and reinforcement learning for robots - 24 lectures, about 29 hours, free.

the homework includes flying a real Crazyflie drone, and the final project is to put a camera on it and train it to navigate by imitation learning, the same learn-from-demos idea robot brains like π0 are built on.

the Fall 2026 lectures go up every week: 11 are out, and lecture 1 already has 84K views.

Lectures (Fall 2026): https://t.co/fatvgSeR16

Slides, notes and homework: https://t.co/Y8adt2clsf

P.S. once you've got the basics, the article below is the 8-week path to building an Optimus-style robot brain at home.

items.title: SHE NEEDS A FAN TO STAY COOL. THAT'S THE MOST REALISTIC PART OF THIS VIDEO. 🤖🌀
items.summary:
SHE NEEDS A FAN TO STAY COOL. THAT'S THE MOST REALISTIC PART OF THIS VIDEO. 🤖🌀

a robot expo. a crowd of phones. 
a girl with a glowing metal core where her waist should be. ✨
someone holds a little fan to it. she smiles, fixes her hair. 

the face? almost certainly AI. 
the fan? that's real robotics. 🔥
every motor, every battery, every AI chip makes heat. 🌡️
heat is one of the reasons real humanoids still work in short shifts and spend hours on chargers. 

so how far have robots actually come? 👇

📅 2015: at the DARPA challenge, robots fell over opening doors.
🤸 2025: humanoids do flips, box, and dance at expos.
📦 2025: Unitree shipped 5,500+ humanoids. AgiBot's CEO said 5,000+.
🇺🇸 Tesla, Figure and Agility: about 150 each (Omdia).
🏭 Hyundai plans a factory for 30,000 robots a year by 2028.

💰 Morgan Stanley: a $5 trillion humanoid market by 2050.
ten years from falling over to doing backflips. 
but the robots that exist are still grey, bulky and plugged in. 🔌

the "robot girl" is what the hype looks like.
the fan is what the engineering looks like. 🛠️
when the real ones catch up with this video, will you be able to tell the difference? 👀
